docs.title: Plugmix for FontLab
docs.text:
Use App-based menu scripts for reporter overlays, or the retained compatibility package for its separate reporter, Filter, Palette, Tool and General runtime. The recovered source preserves both histories; they are not consolidated.

The App menu-script catalogue accounts for all 39 reporter launchers and the menu installer. The compatibility package retains all 19 reporters and the other plugin kinds. Read installation before choosing a runtime, and development and limits before relying on native behavior. LICENSE and NOTICE retain the Apache and MIT terms.

Choose one runtime per FontLab session. Both can create Plugmix menus and use fontlab-plugmix.json; their startup installers and saved preferences are not interchangeable. Native cross-runtime migration and recovery remain unqualified.

This complete local source/generated website does not publish private Pages. Its configured URL is the future repository identity only. Builds import neither plugin runtime and do not start or drive FontLab.

docs.title: App menu-script catalogue
docs.text:
All 39 launchers below live in Scripts/Reports/ and call App's fontlabapp.plugmix, not fontlab_plugmix. They enable the named reporter in every Glyph window; the matching View > Plugmix: Show action disables it. They do not edit font geometry. App owns discovery, painter registration, preference saves, rollback and teardown.

Scripts/Plugmix/Install Plugmix Menu.py is the fortieth recovered file: it installs the App menu and restores saved plugin choices without enabling an additional reporter. The two runtimes' startup paths must not be combined.

Launcher filename Overlay and limits All Angles.py Angle of each straight segment from vertical, mod 180°; components excluded Anchor Cloud.py Names and positions of the current glyph's anchors (local anchors only) Angled Handles.py Rings on handles off the horizontal, vertical and italic axes Blindfold.py Opaque blocks hide the strip from 70 units under the descender up to the baseline, and everything from x-height up to 70 units over the ascender (band = "cap_height" for cap height); the band between baseline and that height stays visible Center Lines.py Advance/2, x-height/2 and cap-height/2 lines Color Toner.py Each component filled in translucent black (darken = 0.15, wrapped into 0..1) so composed parts stand out from drawn outlines Crosshair.py Long guides through selected nodes; no mouse tracking Duplicate Anchor Rings.py Red/yellow rings for every anchor pair less than one unit apart Emphasise Selected Handles.py Accent lines and rings for handles next to selected nodes Glyph Focus.py Shade outside the advance box between descender and ascender Imprecise Italic Angle.py Straight segments within 2° of the slant but not on it Kern Indicator.py Displayed kerning of the pairs touching the glyph, above each junction (orange positive, blue negative); shown only between 3% and 90% zoom Node Count.py Total on- and off-curve nodes; components excluded Node Indexes.py Contour index beside every node Nodes Close to Zones.py Rings on on-curves near zone edges or metric heights Off-curve Handles Outside Bounds.py Handles beyond the on-curve bounding rectangle RSB Line.py Advance boundary with RSB and LSB labels Rekha Viewer.py Head-line bar for Devanagari, Bengali and Gurmukhi letters, moved by rekha and rekha_stop anchors; suffixed or interrupted anchors are not supported Segment Length.py Straight and flattened curve lengths Selected Node Coordinates.py Coordinates beside selected nodes Show Background.py Outlines of the glyph's background layer filled in pale blue (alpha 0.3), counters open; background components are not shown Show Character.py The glyph's first Unicode as 100 px text above the glyph; hidden below 20% zoom; no base-name lookup Show Export Status.py Red cross over the body of a glyph that is set not to export Show Global Glyph.py Contours of a helper glyph named _global behind every other glyph: closed paths orange outline with faint fill, open paths blue outline with faint fill; its components are not shown and it is not drawn on itself Show Glyphs In Label Color.py Glyph and component outlines filled in the mark colour, counters open Show Interpolation.py For each other compatible master, the glyph blended halfway (factor = 0.5) node by node between the shown layer and that master, filled in dark magenta (alpha 0.25), counters open; components are not drawn (neither the shown layer's nor the masters'); no instances, anchors or recentering, and masters with the same coordinates are skipped Show Kerning Group Reference.py Members of the glyph's left kerning class drawn on top of each other as small (0.2) teal silhouettes 150 units left of the glyph, and of its right class 150 units right of it, baseline at half x-height; opacity is 0.8 divided by the class size (floor 0.04), so crowded classes read denser. Left-to-right text only. Very large classes are truncated: at most 32 glyphs are requested, alternating left and right Show Label Color.py Bar in the glyph's mark colour under the descender (placement baseline or body), slanted by the italic angle; layer marks are not distinguished Show Rotated.py Outline turned 180° about its bounds centre; components excluded Show Siblings.py Look-alike Latin letters (c/e/o, b/p, d/q/u, h/l/n/r/a) filled in green behind the glyph, fainter in larger groups; Latin groups only Show Stems.py Rings and span widths along a scan line at half x-height; components excluded Smart Plumblines.py Centre lines through each contour's and the selection's extents; components excluded Smooth Node Angles.py Handle-angle mismatch and length ratio at smooth nodes Speed Punk.py Colour-ramped curvature comb; components excluded Stem Thickness.py Wherever the mouse is (no proximity limit), a line across the outline from the outline point nearest it, perpendicular to it, to the nearer crossing more than 1 unit away, labelled with its rounded length; nothing at a corner where the ray runs along the outline; own contours only, no guide command or modifier key Tops and Bottoms.py Rings and y labels at the highest and lowest on-curves Two Point Distance.py Segment, length and angle for exactly two selected nodes Unitizer.py Vertical grid at UPM / 18 Vertical Metrics.py Labelled ascender, descender, x-height, cap-height and baseline

docs.title: Painting and acceptance limits
docs.text: Center Lines, Vertical Metrics, Crosshair, Tops and Bottoms, RSB Line, Unitizer, Node Count, Smart Plumblines, Show Stems, Speed Punk, Show Rotated, Show Label Color, Show Glyphs In Label Color, Show Character, Rekha Viewer, Show Background, Color Toner, Show Global Glyph, Show Siblings, Show Kerning Group Reference and Show Interpolation draw under the native glyph layer when native canvas painters are available; the rest draw over it, and on older builds all draw over the canvas. The original seven reporters, native canvas drawing and all 18 pre-revision reporters were checked in FontLab 9; Glyph Focus and the revised slant and unit grid have offline coverage only. Node Count, All Angles, Smart Plumblines, Show Stems, Speed Punk, Show Rotated, Blindfold, Show Label Color, Show Glyphs In Label Color, Show Character, Rekha Viewer, Show Export Status, Show Background, Color Toner, Show Global Glyph, Show Siblings, Show Kerning Group Reference, Kern Indicator, Show Interpolation and Stem Thickness have offline test coverage only.

docs.title: App reporter contract
docs.text:
Write a reporter by subclassing fontlabapp.plugmix.Reporter with a unique name, a title and a pure compute(snapshot) that returns Mark objects (ring, line, polyline, polygon, text) in glyph units; pixel sizes are view pixels. Set layer = "background" to paint under the glyph layer. An error raised by compute or requested_glyphs goes to the error sink once per reporter and message until Plugmix is uninstalled. Every snapshot also carries identity (name, Unicodes, raw mark, mark RGB, export flag) and view.px_per_unit; either is None when it cannot be read, and the read error goes to the plugin error sink once. Mark RGB uses HSL lightness 0.65, so it differs slightly from FontLab's flag swatches (inferred, unverified natively). Offline coverage only. Opt-in class flags add costlier data: needs_components gives components (base name, transform and decomposed base contours, nested up to 8 levels), needs_background gives background (the mask's contours, () when empty, None when there is none), and needs_masters gives masters (each master's contours, anchors, advance and a compatible flag that compares contour count, node count per contour and on/off-curve pattern with the shown layer, ignoring components and open/closed state). Components and masters are cached per glyph revision and shared by all reporters; components also re-check their base glyphs. Master outlines may lag until the foreground glyph's lastModified moves, which is unverified natively. The background is read on every paint. An empty component layer means the master that owns the shown layer. Metrics also come from that master. Zones and the italic angle need a master switch to read, so when the shown layer belongs to another master the zones are empty and the italic slant is the current master's. Skipped components and failed reads go to the error sink once. Offline coverage only. needs_kerning gives kerning_groups (the classes used when the glyph is a pair's first member, left, and second member, right, with their members), read on every paint because a class edit may not move the glyph's timestamp. Override requested_glyphs(identity, kerning_groups=None) to name up to 32 other glyphs; others maps each one that exists to its own unselected contours (components skipped), cached per requested glyph's revision. Both use the master that owns the shown layer. needs_neighbours gives view.neighbours: the previous and next glyph on the same line as (name, kerning), kerning in font units as displayed (0 when kerning processing is off). Which glyph stores a pair's kerning is inferred, unverified natively. Neighbours need the native canvas painter backend; with EditorPainters, or when the view scale is unusable, they are None. Offline coverage only. needs_mouse gives view.mouse, the cursor in the glyph's own units (canvas.mousePosition() mapped back through the glyph and text-block transforms), or None when the map is not invertible. While any enabled reporter asks for it, one event filter watches the active glyph window and flushes (updateScreenRect plus updateViewport) at most once per 16 ms after mouse moves, ending with a flush after the last move. The filter goes when the last such reporter is disabled, when the active canvas changes or closes, and on uninstall(). Only the watched canvas gets a mouse; with EditorPainters it is None. Whether moves reach the filter under every tool is unverified natively. Offline coverage only. Third-party packages publish plugin classes in the fontlabapp.plugmix entry-point group.

Historical App native observations do not qualify activation or rendering of this recovered forty-file tuple. Issue 211 native probes remain separate.

docs.title: Compatibility package
docs.text:
src/fontlab_plugmix/ remains a separate installable package with 19 reporters, an undoable Filter, a dockable Palette, a native Tool and a General menu command. Its code, tests, dependencies, startup snippet and legal attribution are retained.

For this runtime, install the package and fontlab-fontlabapp in FontLab's Python 3.11 environment. The optional initScript-snippet.py calls fontlab_plugmix.install() once per session; it remains the compatibility startup snippet, whereas the menu scripts above now target App. Neither file modifies an installation. Use native MeVisLab PythonQt inside FontLab, without another Qt binding. Native per-canvas painters are preferred, with App's EditorPainters fallback on older builds.

The compatibility View menu has 19 Plugmix: Show … actions and Zoom to Selection. Glyph has Delete Small Paths; Window has Step and Repeat Panel and Tool Smart Select. Choices live in FontLab's Data directory as fontlab-plugmix.json. install(config_dir=...) selects an owned directory for tests, and boot.uninstall() removes owned actions, overlays and panels while retaining saved choices. Unknown preference keys survive. The compatibility runtime maps old nodes_outside_paths choices to offcurve_outside_bounds; this is not a cross-runtime migration guarantee.

Filter, Tool and General choices default on until explicitly changed. Palettes start hidden. Saved preferences retain enabled, enabled_filters, enabled_palettes, enabled_tools, enabled_general and last-used params.

docs.title: Compatibility reporters
docs.text:
Reporter Overlay Duplicate Anchor Rings Red/yellow rings for every unordered anchor pair less than one font unit apart; three coincident anchors produce three ring pairs. Node Indexes Full contour index beside every on- and off-curve node. Selected Node Coordinates Coordinates beside selected nodes. Two Point Distance A segment, length and angle for exactly two selected nodes. Off-curve Handles Outside Bounds Off-curve handles beyond the on-curve bounding rectangle. This uses bounds, unlike mekkablue's ShowNodesOutsidePaths path-containment test. Center Lines Advance/2, x-height/2 and cap-height/2 lines. Vertical Metrics Labelled ascender, descender, x-height, cap-height and baseline lines. Angled Handles Rings on off-curve handles outside horizontal, vertical and italic axes. Crosshair Thin, far-reaching guides through selected nodes; no mouse tracking. Tops and Bottoms Rings and y labels at tied highest and lowest on-curve positions. Segment Length Straight and flattened curve lengths where both on-curve ends are selected, or all when nothing is selected; runs of more than two off-curves are skipped. Glyph Focus Translucent shade outside the advance box between descender and ascender. Emphasise Selected Handles Accent lines and rings for handles next to selected nodes; native handles remain visible. Anchor Cloud Names and positions of the current glyph's anchors. RSB Line Advance boundary plus RSB and LSB labels from the native ink box. Unitizer Vertical grid behind the glyph at UPM / 18 increments; units per em is a class attribute. Nodes Close to Zones Rings on on-curves near selected-master zone edges or metric heights. Imprecise Italic Angle Straight segments within 2° of the master slant but not exactly on it. Smooth Node Angles Handle-angle mismatch and handle-length ratio at smooth nodes.

Anchor Cloud shows local anchors only. A font-wide cloud still needs reliable revision-based invalidation. Stroke, text and ring sizes stay constant while zooming. Center Lines, Vertical Metrics, Crosshair, Tops and Bottoms, RSB Line and Unitizer request background painting; older builds substitute foreground painting and log that choice once. Each reporter captures the glyph separately on repaint; zones and native ink bounds are read only when requested.

Native drawing maps glyph points through the glyph text-block transform, the block placement and canvas.mapToViewportF. Text-block placement matters away from the canvas origin. Native compatibility observations are historical; shortcut and keyboard cursor mapping changes still need an in-app recheck.

docs.title: Other compatibility plugins
docs.text:
• Delete Small Paths deletes closed contours below the threshold (default 400 font units squared) using flattened path area or flattened bounds area. Open contours and exact-threshold values stay. It edits selected current-master glyphs through one geometry Undo step, skips automatic layers and unsafe shared/transformed outlines per glyph, and retains safe glyphs in the selection.
  • Step and Repeat duplicates selected contours with count additional copies and repeated X/Y offsets through one geometry Undo step. It retains unselected contours, leaves copies unselected and refuses shared/transformed outlines, non-master display layers, stale contour counts and zero-offset repeats. Count zero or no selection is a no-op. Dock ownership survives temporary hiding; the Window toggle provides explicit close if close detection is absent.
  • Smart Select selects whole contours touched by a dragged rectangle; Shift toggles them. It changes selection only and omits the source plugin's double-click containment and native move handling.
  • Zoom to Selection fits the selected nodes with a margin. It omits delayed viewport adjustment and a shortcut. General font events use stable fgId identities and share the palette host's refresh timer.

docs.title: Write a compatibility reporter
docs.text:
compute() receives immutable Python data and returns marks in font units. Native reads and writes belong in the host layer. Pure imports do not need FontLab:

Reporter.compute(snapshot) receives immutable data and returns Mark objects. Keep this callback pure; no implementation bodies are rendered on this site.

Publish compatibility classes through fontlab_plugmix.plugins entry points. App uses the separate fontlabapp.plugmix group. Names must be unique and titles human-readable. Marks support ring, line, polyline, polygon and text; polygon fill is RGBA, coordinates are font units, and stroke/text/diameter values are view pixels. layer = "background" requests painting beneath native glyphs on supported builds. Callbacks contain failures; reporter compute/paint must not write font data.

docs.title: Development and limits
docs.text:
Use arm64 Python 3.11 and an owned App source. The exact full recipe is:

UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE=only-system PLUGMIX_FONTLABAPP_SOURCE="$PWD/../fontlab-fontlabapp" sh test.sh

The existing runner-layout test also requires that sibling App source directory. The no-selector run executes all tests and checks every compatibility production module for at least 80% line coverage. Arguments skip that checker. To measure the complete recovered script surface with branches as well, run the full suite:

UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE=only-system PLUGMIX_FONTLABAPP_SOURCE="$PWD/../fontlab-fontlabapp" sh test.sh --cov=Scripts --cov-branch --cov-report=json:coverage.json

Recovery tests use real App discovery/boot/registry with existing fake host owners and temporary preferences. They execute all forty files, repeat installation, toggle reporters through menus and check rollback on a preference-save failure. These ordinary checks do not establish native rendering, owner installation, installed artifact contents or publication. Keep the ordinary installed pre-push gate active; its current selector alone does not measure Plugmix's Scripts.

docs.title: Remaining architecture and acceptance
docs.text: Issue 210's future fontlabapp.plugins framework and Extensions bundles are not implemented by this recovery. Specify the bundle/manifest contract first, then qualify discovery, all four plugin kinds, duplicate registration, reload, callbacks, ownership teardown and preservation-safe startup fixtures. Replace reporter-per-script activation only after self-registration qualifies. Issue 211's nine native probes and four minor fixes remain open. Issue 123 remains paused. Further removal of the compatibility surface requires a full consumer, distribution, source-recovery and licence audit. Website work is a later milestone.

docs.title: Website checks
docs.text:
Use a separate Python 3.13 environment and uv 0.13.7, installing the exact hash-locked src_docs/requirements.txt. Run sh src_docs/build.sh and python -m unittest discover -s tests_docs -v. These checks build complete catalogue pages without importing App or Plugmix. The build captures the source commit's timestamp once and both main-triggered jobs use it. A generated output child must be a direct docs-only child of the source SHA with identical non-doc source. The read-only second job checks the actual immutable output and requires full tracked and untracked parity.

The existing 166-test recovery result and retained 68 compatibility/recovery source contracts remain separate historical source qualification. No product code, fixtures, startup script, recovery hash pin or licence is changed by this site. Publication, owner installation and native FontLab rendering remain separate. Private Pages configuration, permissions and requests stay owner-held.

docs.title: App menu scripts
docs.text:
Install the reviewed fontlab-fontlabapp package through the owner-managed FontLab Python 3.11 arm64 environment. Run Scripts/Plugmix/Install Plugmix Menu.py from FontLab's Script menu, then choose a reporter or run one of the 39 Scripts/Reports/ launchers. The menu installer restores saved choices and does not select another reporter. Without saved enabled reporter choices, reporters remain disabled.

Each reporter launcher installs App's menu runtime, enables its named reporter and persists that choice. Use its View > Plugmix: Show action to turn it off. No launcher edits font geometry, installs a Python package or changes the startup file. These source scripts are not included in the compatibility wheel. Duplicate Anchor Rings preserves the source's editable HANDLE_SIZE choices 5, 8 or 12.

docs.title: Compatibility package
docs.text:
From an authorized checkout, install the compatibility package and its App dependency in the owner-managed FontLab Python 3.11 arm64 environment. In an isolated ordinary development environment, the package can be installed with uv pip install . once the required App distribution is available. Use native MeVisLab PythonQt inside FontLab, without another Qt binding.

initScript-snippet.py is an optional compatibility startup snippet: it calls fontlab_plugmix.install() once per session. It does not target App's fontlabapp.plugmix runtime and does not modify an installation. No documentation build installs into FontLab's user folder.

docs.title: Runtime and preference ownership
docs.text:
Choose one runtime per session. Do not combine their startup installers or assume a preference migration guarantee. The shared filename is fontlab-plugmix.json in FontLab's Data directory. install(config_dir=...) selects an owned test directory. Runtime uninstall removes its owned actions, overlays and panels while retaining saved choices. Unknown preference keys survive; failed preference saves roll back activation. Preserve failed-teardown recovery rather than treating a partial teardown as success.

Filter, Tool and General choices default on until explicitly changed; palettes start hidden. Saved choices retain enabled, enabled_filters, enabled_palettes, enabled_tools, enabled_general and last-used params. The compatibility rename from nodes_outside_paths to offcurve_outside_bounds is an internal migration only.

docs.title: Licence and attribution
docs.text:
The repository retains Apache-2.0 terms and the Apache-2.0/MIT source-specific attribution in its NOTICE. The App-based menu scripts and compatibility package retain their own source history; the website does not add a new grant for upstream implementation bodies.

  • Download the exact repository LICENSE.
  • Download the exact repository NOTICE.

All product source and retained attribution remain unchanged. The MaterialX frontend also retains its bundled third-party licences and notices in generated assets. No Fly product licence has been copied here.
